result.title: BenchMint: From Real-World Tasks to Executable Benchmarks
result.comment: Supplementary analysis and reproducibility materials are included as ancillary files
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) need evaluations of everyday reasoning and tool use, such as planning itineraries under user constraints and grounding numerical answers in evidence. We introduce BenchMint, an automated benchmark-construction workflow, and Daily-Life, its collection of 100 selected tasks across 11 real-world domains. BenchMint jointly constructs tasks and scoring criteria from the same source documents. Language-model judges assess possible answers against these criteria using tool traces and private evidence. We report 26 model/harness configurations, including GPT, Claude and Gemini families; 17 have complete domain profiles. These are descriptive configuration results, not a controlled model ranking. In one selected travel task, we corrected the reference total from 320 to 380 minutes while keeping both answers unchanged. The incorrect answer's arithmetic verdict switched from pass to fail; the correct answer's switched from fail to pass. With one ballot per cell, this exposes a reference error without establishing repeatability or collection-wide validity. Incomplete construction comparisons establish no general advantage of joint authoring or feedback-guided revision.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BenchMint 自动基准构建流程，从同一来源文档联合生成任务与评分标准，并构建覆盖 11 个日常领域的 100 个任务集 Daily-Life，由语言模型评审结合工具轨迹与私有证据打分，报告 26 种配置的结果并分析参考答案错误。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「同一来源联合生成任务与评分准则」及基于证据、工具轨迹的评审协议，可能为 LVR 评价中的证据定位与判分设计提供可核查线索，但不涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理。
